explanation: When you multiply powers of the same base, add the exponents. When you divide, subtract them. When you raise a power to another power, multiply the exponents. A negative exponent tells you to divide, so it subtracts from the total.
workedExample: Simplify $2^3 \times 2^2$. Same base, so add the exponents: $2^{3+2} = 2^5 = 32$. The base stays $2$ — only the exponents combine.
